title: Report a WideCast problem to the WideCast team
description:
Synchronous, no credit. Report a problem with WideCast itself — a failing
upload, a broken export, an overlay that will not build, an endpoint
returning a 5xx you cannot work around. The report is emailed straight to
the WideCast team.

This is NOT a user-notification channel: to tell the USER something, use
POST /v1/notification/send instead. And it is not for content problems you
can fix yourself (a weak hook, a wrong background, a typo) — only for
WideCast malfunctioning.

Whenever the failing call returned a request_id, put it in context. It is
the single most useful field for tracing a report back to the server log.

fields.name: error_message
fields.label: Error message (required — what went wrong; prefer the verbatim error text; max 4000 chars)

fields.name: module
fields.label: module (optional — which part failed; defaults to 'agent'; max 80 chars)

fields.name: context
fields.label: context — optional debugging details (object). Include the failing call's request_id.

use_cases.title: 🚩 Minimal report
use_cases.description: Just the error text. module defaults to 'agent'. Returns {object:'error_report', reported:true, module, context_keys, request_id}.

request.error_message: video_data returned 502 script_parse_failed on a video that renders fine in the editor

use_cases.title: 🔎 Report with tracing context (recommended)
use_cases.description: The shape you should aim for: name the module, paste the verbatim error, and include the failing call's request_id plus the ids you were working on. This is what makes a report actionable.

context.attempted: second export retry after scene 4 edit

use_cases.title: 🎬 Scene-level failure
use_cases.description: Reporting a per-scene problem — pass voice_file and scene_id so the team can reproduce on the exact scene.

request.error_message: upload_failed: 413 payload too large after auto-compression
